findings.issue: Escrow release has no owner across the notes. A37 says escrow.release is A39's (A16's catalogue names A39 as caller) and dropped postEscrowRelease. A38 also says A39 owns it. But A39 says it 'never creates an escrow.release approval or posts an escrow.release journal (A38 F4 owns both, through A37's postEscrowRelease)'. A39 also has no dependency on A37, although A37 names A39 as the caller of getEscrowReleaseBasis and of the refund-batch reads. Built as written, nobody drafts or posts escrow.release, and A39 cannot import A37's interface.
findings.fix: Add a recorded loop on A39 to A37's 'Loops this spec requires' list: A39 owns the escrow.release approval, effector and journal (as A16 and A38 already say), calls A37.getEscrowReleaseBasis, and drops the postEscrowRelease sentence. Add A37 to A39's deps in app-graph.json. There is no cycle, because A39 is not an ancestor of A37.

findings.issue: The A37/A38 contract still diverges in ways loop A38.1 does not list. The current A38 text: (1) calls lockAllocation as the drafter, where A37 makes requestAllocationLock the drafter and lockAllocation the internal effector; (2) spells the revert approval code offer.revert_and_refund, where A37 has offer.revert (A36 uses both); (3) spells the refund approval code orders.refund.batch, where A37 has order.refund.batch; (4) uses the reason words scaled_back, excluded_at_allocation and offering_cancelled, against A37's enum scale_back, excluded_at_mint and revert; (5) takes the refund fee leg 'from fee_payable_realx', where A37 and A16 take the fee out of the order's own escrow sub-balance; (6) calls settle(order_id, {register_entry_id, register_version_id, token_delivery}), where A37's signature takes allocation_id, file_sha256, custody_op_id and recon_run_id; (7) calls excludeAllocationLine(..., approval_id), where A37's last argument is ctx. A38 also asks A37 to confirm the approval_id argument, and to confirm that computeRefundBatch can run while SM-04 is closed; A37 answers neither. The AUTO check is keyed on the revert approval's action code, so it will fail on the spelling alone.
findings.fix: Extend loop A38.1 to list each of these items explicitly. Pick one spelling for each code: recommend offer.revert_and_refund, which A38 seeds in A03/A14, and order.refund.batch or the A03 action id for row 12. State whether excludeAllocationLine takes an approval_id for point-2 and point-3 exclusions. State that computeRefundBatch may run while SM-04 is closed, so its hash can go into the revert approval.

findings.issue: The AUTO refund path cannot pass A16's approval binding. A16's order.refund row binds approvals by the object refund_batch:<id> ('AUTO on refund_batch:<id> when the refund file hash equals the approved one') and refuses any mismatch by object or action code. A37 posts each order.refund journal with approval_id set to the offer.revert approval, whose object is the offering. On a failed raise (J05), every refund journal would be refused with LDG_APPROVAL_MISMATCH, so the 37-order failed-raise challenge cannot pass.
findings.fix: Under AUTO, A37 raises an A14 order.refund.batch request on refund_batch:<id>. It resolves to A14's AUTO row with auto_condition file_sha256_equals_approved and references the approved revert approval that carries the batch hash. The journals are posted with that AUTO approval id. Add a challenge that posts with the revert approval id directly and expects LDG_APPROVAL_MISMATCH.

findings.issue: SM-05 transitions contradict A03's frozen guard table, and loop A03.1 covers only awaiting_funds -> cancelled. (1) eligibility_check__reflection_period and eligibility_check__awaiting_funds use the guard retail_regime_p2 ('so a retail P2 order can never skip the reflection period'), but A37 sends retail orders with cooling_off_days = 0, its default, to awaiting_funds. (2) funded__refund_pending requires offer_failed_or_zero_allocation, but A37 also uses it for investor_cancelled, material_change_not_reconfirmed and deposit_returned while the offering is live. (3) allocated__refund_pending requires partial_allocation (0 < allocated < ordered), but A37 uses it only for a full exclusion (allocated 0) and never for a partial allocation. (4) reflection_period__awaiting_funds requires reflection_ended, but A37 also fires it at an early close. (5) refund_pending__refunded requires linked_approval_closed on row 12 (Issue refund), but the AUTO path runs under row 10 and moves the order during execution, before the approval is closed. A03's runner will refuse these transitions, or the builder will bypass the guards.
findings.fix: Widen loop A03.1, with A03's owner, to the full list of guard changes: retail reflection only when cooling_off_days > 0; funded__refund_pending extended to investor cancel, a lapsed material-change window and a returned deposit; allocated__refund_pending allowing allocated = 0 on exclusion; reflection_period__awaiting_funds when the offering closes; refund_pending__refunded accepting row 10 under AUTO and an approved or executing approval. Alternatively, change A37 to fit the existing guards. Add a challenge that runs every A37 transition through A03's runner with guards on.

findings.issue: G12 is implemented twice, and a client can fake 'opened'. A35 owns the only acknowledgement store: A04's core document_acknowledgement table, of which A04 says 'A37's disclosure_acknowledgements is this table'. A35 derives opened_at only from server-side document_open rows, rejects any client-supplied opened_at, owns standing_consent and the CQ-02 standing-consent evaluator, and exports recordAcknowledgements(tx, ...) for A37's placement transaction. A37 instead creates its own disclosure_acknowledgement table, accepts acknowledgements: [{document_id, version, sha256, opened_at}] in the POST body, and gates standing consent with its own orders.agent_standing_consent config key read from A12's mandate. A12 also says standing consent never covers a person's first purchase in a trust; A37 has no such rule. Any API caller could bypass the product map's rule 'Documents not opened: confirm stays disabled'.
findings.fix: Drop the disclosure_acknowledgement module table and the orders.agent_standing_consent key. At placement, call A35's recordAcknowledgements(tx, {holderId, offeringId, orderRef, documentVersionIds, statementHash, actor}) inside the order transaction, so opened_at comes from A35's document_open rows. Take documents_required from A35's getDisclosureSet. For agents, use the CQ-02 parameter and the standing_consent row that A35 and A12 own, including the first-purchase exclusion. Add a challenge: a POST that carries opened_at for an unopened document is rejected by the schema and no order is created.

findings.issue: The gate sets that A37 renders and tests contradict A19's table 3, which A19's oracle asserts byte for byte. A19: order = G01 G02 G03 G04 G05 G06 G07 G10 G11 G12 G14 G16 G21; order_allocation = G01 G02 G04 G05 G07 G10 G11 G14 G21. A37: order = G01 G04 G06 G07 G11 G12 G21; allocation = 'the same minus G11 and G12', i.e. G01 G04 G06 G07. At placement A37 omits G02 (sanctions), G03 (KYB), G10 (halt), G14 (AML) and G16 (tax). At allocation it adds G06 and drops G02, G10, G11, G14 and G21. A37's tests would fail against the real A19, and its oracle and challenges would never check that a sanctions hit or a halt excludes an order at allocation. A19 also names A37 as the provider of G07's open_order_units fact ('submitted or funded, unallocated, unrefunded'). A37 never registers that provider, and the definition leaves out awaiting_funds, although A37's G07 vector depends on counting an earlier unfunded order.
findings.fix: Replace both lists with 'A19 table 3, rows order and order_allocation', and assert the rows A19 returns instead of a local list. Register a G07 open_order_units fact provider through registerFactProvider. Define open units as orders in submitted, eligibility_check, reflection_period, awaiting_funds, or funded and not yet allocated or refunded, and loop A19 to match. Add challenges: a G02 hit and a G10 halt at allocation each exclude and refund the order.

findings.issue: Route scopes and approval codes are not valid identifiers on this platform. A09's route registration throws on a scope id that is not in A03's scopes.ts. A12 defines scopeId === A03 action id, with the grammar <PREFIX>.<object>.<verb> (for example INV.order.place, M05.allocation.lock). A37 uses orders:quote, orders:place, orders:cancel, orders:read, orders:allocate, offerings:read and treasury:read, and none of them exist. Every route will fail registration, or the builder will invent a mapping that decides what agents may do. The approval action codes orders.allocation.lock and order.refund.batch are not seeded in A03 or A14 either, since 'Allocate' has no D07 maker-checker row. Unlike A38, this spec records no A03/A14 seeding loop, so A14's policy resolver has no row for the lock request.
findings.fix: Map every route to its A03 action id (for example INV.order.quote, INV.order.place, INV.order.cancel, INV.order.read, M05.allocation.preview, M05.allocation.lock, M05.refund.submit, SPN.offer.read) and list the ids with the routes. Add a recorded A03/A14 loop that seeds the lock row (CAPM to CFO, 4E, the ADM-12 'Allocate' action) and ties the refund-batch code to row 12 'Issue refund' (FINA to CFO, 4E), with an AUTO row for the revert path.

findings.issue: G11 at placement ignores A36's over-subscription ceiling. A36 caps acceptance at acceptance_ceiling_units, which is hard_cap_units + floor(hard_cap_units x oversubscription_cap_bps / 10,000) for pro_rata and exactly the hard cap for first_come, and exports it in G11's offer_state fact. A37's rule accepts any order once allow_oversubscription is on, and its OfferingTerms list leaves out oversubscription_cap_bps. A build that follows A37 can take unbounded money into escrow.
findings.fix: Add oversubscription_cap_bps (or acceptance_ceiling_units) to the parameters A37 reads. State G11 as units <= acceptance_ceiling_units - Σ open units, flagging may_be_scaled_back above the hard cap. Add boundary vectors at the ceiling and at the ceiling + 1.

findings.issue: The replay after a 428 does not follow A12's execution-time rule. A12 says: 'A confirmed action counts toward the day's and the month's totals, and the daily and monthly checks run again under the counter lock when it executes; if they fail then, it is refused 403 G22_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.' A37's orders.placement_replay only re-checks that the token and mandate are live. SM-05 defines no outcome for an order already committed in 'submitted' that fails the caps, a hold or a kill switch at replay.
findings.fix: In orders.placement_replay, re-run A12's daily and monthly checks under the counter lock and count the order toward the totals. On failure, move the order submitted -> cancelled with cancel_reason agent_limit_exceeded, adding that value to the enum and to loop A03.1. Add a vector where the daily cap is used up between the 428 and the passkey.

findings.issue: The clean-reconciliation precondition before allocation is optional: it applies only 'when the provider is wired', and ReconStatusProvider stays a fake until A38 wires it. The graph now makes A20 an ancestor of A37, and A20's blocking matrix already refuses 'allocation' while a cash break is open (A39 says A37 and A38 call assertClear). A37 can pass its gate without the recon check ever running.
findings.fix: Call A20's assertClear(vehicleId, 'allocation') directly in requestAllocationLock and in the lock effector. Keep the provider only for settle's run lookup, if it is still needed. Add a challenge with an open cash break and zero Δ; the lock must be refused.
